about: R27 review ledger (D110). One entry per safety-class Spanish string: the exact English, the exact Spanish, sha = sha256(en + U+0000 + es), and how far its review has got — draft (written), reviewed (blind second pass agreed AND back-translated to English without the original), person (a Spanish-reading crew member read it on a phone, R27 #5 / R29 #3). Safety-class Spanish is served only at reviewed or person. Editing either side without re-reviewing fails the build (src/i18n/ledger.ts ledgerProblems).

entries.es: NO LO MANEJE NI LO USE — FUERA DE SERVICIO (FRENOS O DIRECCIÓN)
entries.translatedBy: Claude — proposed in D112 (2026-10-22) after the blind review found drift in the plan table’s "NO SE MANEJA — FRENOS/DIRECCIÓN"; applied in D112’s held-five round
entries.reviewedBy: Two blind passes, 2026-10-22 (D112’s held-five round): a second translation of the English alone (never saw this Spanish) and a back-translation of this Spanish alone (never saw the English) — two agents with no tools, neither saw the other side; compared by Claude.
entries.backTranslation: DO NOT DRIVE IT OR USE IT — OUT OF SERVICE (BRAKES OR STEERING)
entries.note: Recorded 2026-10-22 (D112) — the held-five round. Back: same meaning — out of service, with the order that state puts on a crew (do not drive it or use it) and the reason (brakes or steering: the only thing that holds a unit, src/fleet/breakdown.ts, R26). Second (the English alone): "RETENIDO — FUERA DE SERVICIO" — held, out of service: the same meaning; D112’s first blind second, "NO CONDUZCA — FUERA DE SERVICIO", agrees too. Flagged and accepted: "manejar" is handle in some places — "NI LO USE" bans both readings; the brackets carry no verb and do not say which of the two failed — the English badge says neither (the Fleet card’s line names "brake/steering defect"); the order allows no short move — it errs toward stopping, and only Mike signs the unit back on; "dirección" is also address or direction — beside FRENOS and MANEJE it reads as steering. Replaces the plan’s "NO SE MANEJA — FRENOS/DIRECCIÓN" (D112: drift — it can read as a description, not an order), which is no longer in the repo.

entries.en: PERMIT LIKELY — do not start protected work until the permit is confirmed.
entries.es: PROBABLEMENTE SE NECESITA PERMISO — no empiece el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work) hasta que se confirme el permiso.
entries.translatedBy: Claude — R27 Phase A unit 1, first translation pass (D111)
entries.reviewedBy: Three blind passes (D112’s protected-work round): D111’s review-round second translation (2026-10-22 — the English alone, taken out before the builder’s Spanish was read; it wrote “en zona protegida” for “protected work”), the held-five round’s back-translation of this Spanish alone (2026-10-22 — never saw the English), and the protected-work round’s second translation (2026-10-22 — the English and the binding glossary alone, never saw this Spanish; it agreed); agents with no tools, no pass saw another’s side; compared by Claude.
entries.backTranslation: A PERMIT IS PROBABLY NEEDED — do not start the work that requires a permit (protected work) until the permit is confirmed.
entries.note: Recorded 2026-10-22 (D112) — the protected-work round; held twice before (D112, the held-five round). Second (the protected-work round — the English and the binding glossary alone): this Spanish word for word — the headline is the glossary’s recorded PERMIT LIKELY label and "el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work)" its trade term, both given; "no empiece … hasta que se confirme el permiso" is the pass’s own and the same. Back (D112 and the held-five round, both blind): no drift — the hedge on the need, the prohibition firm. The two earlier forward passes differed from this Spanish only on "protected work" (D111: "en zona protegida" — a narrower meaning, src/permitting/permitRecord.ts requiresClearance also counts a permit flag outside any zone; the held-five round: "el trabajo protegido" — the rendering the glossary rules out); the term rests on the glossary (src/i18n/glossary.ts TRADE_TERMS, D111 UI 5), and this round’s forward pass, given it as D112 named owed, agrees on everything else. Flagged and accepted (as before): "permiso" is also permission — the headline and "requiere permiso" frame it as a permit; "hasta que se confirme" names no one — the English names no one; "until it is confirmed whether one is needed" still stops; which work is meant — the English "protected work" asks the reader the same, and the headline says a permit is probably needed for this job; the English line is shown beneath.

entries.en: NO OVERLAY — VERIFY W/ CITY before protected work.
entries.es: VERIFIQUE CON LA CIUDAD — EL MAPA NO MOSTRÓ ZONA PROTEGIDA. Hágalo antes de empezar el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work).
entries.translatedBy: Claude — R27 Phase A unit 1, first translation pass (D111)
entries.reviewedBy: Three blind passes (D112’s protected-work round): D111’s review-round second translation (2026-10-22 — the English alone, taken out before the builder’s Spanish was read; it wrote “en zona protegida” for “protected work”), the held-five round’s back-translation of this Spanish alone (2026-10-22 — never saw the English), and the protected-work round’s second translation (2026-10-22 — the English and the binding glossary alone, never saw this Spanish; it agreed); agents with no tools, no pass saw another’s side; compared by Claude.
entries.backTranslation: CHECK WITH THE CITY — THE MAP DID NOT SHOW A PROTECTED ZONE. Do it before starting the work that requires a permit (protected work).
entries.note: Recorded 2026-10-22 (D112) — the protected-work round; held twice before (D112, the held-five round). Second (the protected-work round — the English and the binding glossary alone): "VERIFIQUE CON LA CIUDAD — EL MAPA NO MOSTRÓ ZONA PROTEGIDA. Verifique antes de hacer el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work)." — the same meaning: the headline is the glossary’s recorded NO OVERLAY label; "Verifique antes de hacer" names the verb that this Spanish’s "Hágalo antes de empezar" points back to (VERIFIQUE is the only thing the line tells the reader to do), and "empezar" (before starting) is the stricter of the two and the one served. Back (D112 and the held-five round, both blind): no change of meaning. The two earlier forward passes differed from this Spanish only on "protected work" (D111: "en zona protegida" — a narrower meaning, src/permitting/permitRecord.ts requiresClearance also counts a permit flag outside any zone; the held-five round: "el trabajo protegido" — the rendering the glossary rules out); the term rests on the glossary (src/i18n/glossary.ts TRADE_TERMS, D111 UI 5), and this round’s forward pass, given it as D112 named owed, agrees on everything else. The reassurance flag (the held-five round’s back-translator: "EL MAPA NO MOSTRÓ ZONA PROTEGIDA" can read as "no zone, so no permit, so nothing to verify"), judged strictly against how the English reads to an English-only crew member — the Spanish is NOT more reassuring: (1) it leads with the unconditional order VERIFIQUE CON LA CIUDAD, where the English leads with the finding NO OVERLAY; (2) it gives the finding as the map’s ("el mapa no mostró" — the map did not show, also "failed to show"), where the English states it bare; (3) the "no zone, so nothing to verify" reading is the English’s own shape (NO OVERLAY … before protected work) — both blind forward passes wrote "no protected zone on the map" for NO OVERLAY (the held-five round’s, made without the glossary: "SIN CAPA DE ZONA PROTEGIDA EN EL MAPA") — and on that reading the English’s only order is bound to "before protected work" while the Spanish keeps its leading VERIFIQUE; (4) the one difference that cuts the other way — "zona protegida" is plain where "overlay" is jargon, so every Spanish reader understands the finding — is the same fact made legible (the glossary’s overlay is "zona protegida del mapa"), not a stronger claim, and the English is shown beneath. Still open for Mike: whether the line should say the map is not a clearance — an English change first, then a new blind pass of both sides. Also flagged and accepted: "la ciudad" names no office — nor does the English; this state gates no work outside an RPA (src/permitting/permitRecord.ts requiresClearance) — the English is the screen’s advisory, and the Spanish gives it as an order.

entries.en: PERMIT STATUS UNKNOWN — Arbo could not read the permit screen. Check with the office before protected work.
entries.es: ESTADO DEL PERMISO DESCONOCIDO — Arbo no pudo leer el chequeo de permiso. Consulte con la oficina antes de empezar el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work).
entries.translatedBy: Claude — R27 Phase A unit 1, first translation pass (D111)
entries.reviewedBy: Three blind passes (D112’s protected-work round): D111’s review-round second translation (2026-10-22 — the English alone, taken out before the builder’s Spanish was read; it wrote “en zona protegida” for “protected work”), the held-five round’s back-translation of this Spanish alone (2026-10-22 — never saw the English), and the protected-work round’s second translation (2026-10-22 — the English and the binding glossary alone, never saw this Spanish; it agreed); agents with no tools, no pass saw another’s side; compared by Claude.
entries.backTranslation: PERMIT STATUS UNKNOWN — Arbo could not read the permit check. Check with the office before starting the work that requires a permit (protected work).
entries.note: Recorded 2026-10-22 (D112) — the protected-work round; held twice before (D112, the held-five round). Second (the protected-work round — the English and the binding glossary alone): "ESTADO DEL PERMISO DESCONOCIDO — Arbo no pudo leer el chequeo de permiso. Consulte con la oficina antes de hacer el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work)." — this Spanish but for "hacer" (doing) where it says "empezar" (starting): the same order — the office comes first — and the served "empezar" is the stricter. Back (D112 and the held-five round, both blind): no drift. The two earlier forward passes differed from this Spanish only on "protected work" (D111: "en zona protegida" — a narrower meaning, src/permitting/permitRecord.ts requiresClearance also counts a permit flag outside any zone; the held-five round: "el trabajo protegido" — the rendering the glossary rules out); the term rests on the glossary (src/i18n/glossary.ts TRADE_TERMS, D111 UI 5), and this round’s forward pass, given it as D112 named owed, agrees on everything else. Flagged and accepted (as before): "Arbo" may be taken for a person (or "árbol") — the English says Arbo too, and either way the step is the office; "no pudo leer el chequeo" may read as an illegible document rather than a failed lookup — either way the status is unknown and the step is the same; "chequeo" is informal (D110, open for Mike); "consulte con" is check with, as the English says (L13 is recorded with it); which work is meant — as PERMIT LIKELY’s line.

entries.en: PERMIT SCREEN PENDING — status UNKNOWN, no screen on file. Check with the office before protected work.
entries.es: CHEQUEO DE PERMISO SIN HACER — estado DESCONOCIDO, no hay chequeo registrado. Consulte con la oficina antes de empezar el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work).
entries.translatedBy: Claude — R27 Phase A unit 1, first translation pass (D111)
entries.reviewedBy: Three blind passes (D112’s protected-work round): D111’s review-round second translation (2026-10-22 — the English alone, taken out before the builder’s Spanish was read; it wrote “en zona protegida” for “protected work”), the held-five round’s back-translation of this Spanish alone (2026-10-22 — never saw the English), and the protected-work round’s second translation (2026-10-22 — the English and the binding glossary alone, never saw this Spanish; it agreed); agents with no tools, no pass saw another’s side; compared by Claude.
entries.backTranslation: PERMIT CHECK NOT DONE — status UNKNOWN, there is no check on record. Check with the office before starting the work that requires a permit (protected work).
entries.note: Recorded 2026-10-22 (D112) — the protected-work round; held twice before (D112, the held-five round). Second (the protected-work round — the English and the binding glossary alone): "CHEQUEO DE PERMISO SIN HACER — estado DESCONOCIDO, no hay chequeo de permiso registrado. Consulte con la oficina antes de hacer el trabajo que requiere permiso (protected work)." — the same meaning: "no hay chequeo de permiso registrado" spells out the "chequeo" this Spanish’s headline already names; "hacer" for "empezar" as the UNKNOWN line (the served "empezar" the stricter). Back (D112 and the held-five round, both blind): no drift. The two earlier forward passes differed from this Spanish only on "protected work" (D111: "en zona protegida" — a narrower meaning, src/permitting/permitRecord.ts requiresClearance also counts a permit flag outside any zone; the held-five round: "el trabajo protegido" — the rendering the glossary rules out); the term rests on the glossary (src/i18n/glossary.ts TRADE_TERMS, D111 UI 5), and this round’s forward pass, given it as D112 named owed, agrees on everything else. Flagged and accepted (as before): "SIN HACER" may suggest the crew does the check — the line sends them to the office before starting; "no hay chequeo registrado" does not say whether one was ever done — "no screen on file" says no more; it reads close to the UNKNOWN line — both send the crew to the office, the difference is the office’s; "consulte" as the UNKNOWN line; pending is not done (as the glossary label, recorded); which work is meant — as PERMIT LIKELY’s line.
